verdict.rationale: LangSmith documents a Playground service that forwards requests to various LLM APIs and to custom model servers, and its self-hosted docs list prompt engineering as a platform capability. That covers a first-party playground running against real models, but the evidence comes only from self-hosting architecture notes, not from a feature page on prompt iteration. Missing for 10: documentation of template variables/inputs in the playground, an iterative prompt editing or comparison workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can iterate on prompts in a playground against real models and variables

citations.quote: The Playground is a service that handles forwarding requests to various LLM APIs... This can also be used to connect to your own custom model servers.
Host an instance of LangSmith in your own infrastructure for observability, evaluation, and prompt engineering.
